Adventure journal -> Artifacts: original Windows PE source grammar

These are offline original-image sources, not game observations, translated
examples, or checks. tools/extract_adventure_journal_artifacts_pe.py reads the
two images configured in data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. pe-functions.tsv
retains their identities, hashes, real unwind extents and executable extents;
pe-branches/conditions/switches/calls/literals.tsv retain the native operands.
DecompileJournalAgreementsPE.java feeds those original instructions and jump
table overrides into Ghidra. pe-*-ghidra-decompiled.c and the individual .c
files are actual Ghidra output. RVAs below are Steam; corresponding complete
Classic bodies and their independent addresses are recorded in the manifest.

SCREEN OWNERSHIP AND DISPLAY
  viewscreen_adventure_logst renderer c2110..ca4f9, executable end ca358.
  screen+256 is the selected main tab (int16); value 7 selects Artifacts.
  screen+254 is a map blink flag, not the selected tab.
  screen+5a8 is the displayed artifact-card pointer vector, copied/filterable
  from screen+488; screen+2c8 is its first card index. screen+250 is the
  selected card, screen+274 its internal text scroll, screen+278 expanded.
  The Artifacts branch is c84d0..c88bb. No second artifact-card renderer or
  separate pinned-artifact draw exists outside this branch in this owner.

  card+0 points to artifact; artifact+90 points to the concrete item.
  card+8 is full title; card+48 is the clipped title; card+68 is the vector
  of wrapped description-row string pointers. card+80 begins location cache.
  Draw calls: title c8618/return c861d; counter c86be/return c86c3;
  description c8782/return c8787. Classic draw sites are these RVAs minus 70.
  The title and n/total counter occupy top border y. A collapsed card shows
  three body rows y+1..y+3, has bottom border y+4, next card top y+5. A sole
  body row is centered at y+2. Expanded mode hides nonselected bodies and
  gives selected body dimy-((dimy-6)/5)-6 rows. Rows always originate in the
  same native vector, indexed by the selected card's text scroll.
  Selected overflow cards draw a 4-column x 3-row arrow texture block after
  the body text: x=right-4..right-1, y=top+body_capacity-1..+1. This block
  covers source text at the right edge of the last visible body rows. It is
  drawn through adb100, not as an English paragraph. Collapsed branch only
  draws it if the vector has >3 rows; expanded branch always draws it.
  The main list's separate right scrollbar does not own body text.

FULL TITLE SOURCE
  Initializer be410..bfdf0, artifact construction bea88..bebbd.
  It allocates 0xb8-byte cards, initializes their strings/vectors/cache, and
  stores the artifact pointer at +0. If artifact.name.has_name(+7a) is true,
  a946e0(artifact+8,card+8,true,false) writes its English generated name.
  Otherwise it assigns literal "Unknown". Generated names retain all native
  first-name, nickname, compound, adjective, hyphen, noun, Of/POS choices.
  d09e0 copies full title+8 into clipped title+48 when +58 size is zero and
  truncates to 58 source bytes. It never calls b94400 to produce this title.
  Consequently "Untitled", item-name fallback and unknown-artifact branches
  of the shared b94400 helper are not top-title alternatives in this page.
  That helper is still retained as a possible shared-reference text source.

COMPLETE BODY AND COMPOSITION
  Producer d09e0..d14c9 does nothing further if card+68 vector is nonempty.
  On cache miss it calls c75000(artifact.item, dst, true, true, false,0) at
  d0ab7. It wraps the complete returned document to 58 source bytes via
  8e7440 at d0b31, preserving every line beyond the displayed first three.
  R9=true selects plain source spaces rather than paragraph markup. flags=0
  suppresses LPAGE/numeric reference markup. R8=true propagates to artwork;
  it does not disable artwork or restrict the body to opening/material text.

  Complete shared-source closure is data/extracted/item-description-sources.tsv
  and item-description-sources.md. Those cataloged native branches remain
  part of this caller: item type/RAW subtype/material/quantity; artifact or
  ordinary craftsmanship/quality/maker; food ingredients; all improvement
  kinds including bands, rings, spikes, rollers, handle, chain/rope, gemstone
  cuts and materials; base/image/sewn art, historical-art references; dye,
  color, quality and mixture combinations; dice face/series/range/top face;
  every writing carrier, page count, title/no-title, author/no-author, format,
  content subject, style and empty writing branch; coins/ruler/year/faces;
  slab stored inscriptions; wear; contaminants and material states; source
  kind10 power description; tool/instrument RAW and stored descriptions.

  The item graph itself binds its art/history/memorial/item-title/RAW subgraphs
  and every general_ref +90 text-producing virtual owner. It is not replaced
  by a list of screenshot books or by nearby literal strings. Arbitrary world
  names, counts, written work titles, authors, raw/mod descriptions, and stored
  histories are unbounded dynamic fields in these finite native productions.

  This page runs in Adventure context: c77dfd/c7809e/c78e3f literacy/read
  branches guarded by game_mode=1 and active adventurer are reachable here.
  Do not inherit the fortress world-map popup's exclusion of unread/unable-to-
  read text. Writing content, empty pages and slab inscriptions also remain.
  Actual c75000/c65450/cc6a10/cc7020/cc5d50 bodies and the complete style
  leaf cc5520..cc5d50 are retained here. All general_ref suppliers also have
  existing actual Ghidra sources in ../adventure-reading-popup, referenced
  by the shared item catalog.

OPTIONAL LOCATION PARAGRAPH (COMPLETE PRIORITY CHAIN)
  The same producer seeds cache+80 from the artifact, then applies rumors
  9de930 and first-hand observations 9dee30 from the adventurer's knowledge.
  If holder(+90), site(+88), region(+94) and layer(+98) are all -1, no
  location paragraph or blank separator is appended.
  Otherwise prefix is selected in strict order:
    year(+9c)==-1: "It is traditionally thought to be "
    else firsthand(+a8)!=null: "It was last seen "
    else: "It was last rumored to be "

  Location is one mutually exclusive chain:
    holder(+90)!=-1:
      "held by " + historical_figure_display(holder,default_context,1,0)
    else site(+88)!=-1:
      if building(+8c)!=-1:
        site_building_display(site,building,true,flags=0) + " in "
      "in " + surface_region_display(site,flags=0)
    else surface_region(+94)!=-1:
      "in " + surface_region_display(region,flags=0)
    else underground_layer(+98)!=-1:
      "in " + underground_label(layer)

  The site branch really calls b94a40 with cache.site, not b93930. It also
  really emits both adjacent " in " and "in " when a building is present.
  Preserve these original-source shapes instead of guessing a corrected
  English sentence. Historical figure source includes generated names,
  anonymous race/caste, zombie, ghost, transformation and unresolved figure.
  Surface region source includes generated and empty names, and unresolved
  "an unknown region". Underground source: absent pointer -> "an unknown
  underground region"; named-region has_name=true -> empty; unnamed type0
  -> "the depths of the world", type1 -> "the magma sea", type2 -> "the
  Underworld", other types -> empty. Empty fields remain real native branches.

  If year!=-1 append " in " + b92640(year,tick); always append ".".
  b92640 is a calendar formatter, not a place-name formatter. year<1 prints
  "a time before time"; year>=1 and tick==-1 prints the decimal year; else
  "the "+phase+season+" of "+year. phase is "early ", "mid", or "late ";
  season is spring/summer/autumn/winter for tick/100800=0/1/2/3, else empty.
  Phase cutoffs for tick%100800 are 33600 and 67200 (inclusive lower bins).
  A blank separator row and the 58-byte-wrapped full location paragraph are
  appended to the existing card+68 vector. That appended paragraph may be
  offscreen until scrolled, but it is part of this page's source document.

LOCATION KNOWLEDGE PRODUCERS
  9de930 applies rumor.type2 incident state0..5 and types25..33 with their
  native artifact/time/matching-location constraints; other values make no
  visible text. 9dee30 applies first-hand event state0..5 and newer timestamp
  constraints. They update the same five location fields and timestamp, not
  independent text captions. Their full native branches and selectors are
  retained in the manifest and their individual Ghidra .c bodies.
